headline: THE COPY IN THE MUD: glaciers scraped Alaska's eruption record off the land, so three USGS Alaska Volcano Observatory scientists in Anchorage read a surviving copy out of Gulf of Alaska seafloor mud, and the machine could only name a volcano confidently where the volcano had been writing the same chemical signature over and over
primary_source: Lubbers, Loewen and Wallace, Geochemistry Geophysics Geosystems vol 27 issue 7, July 2026, doi 10.1029/2026GC013096
reported_elsewhere: none, this is an unreported scoop

what_is_already_done: claims.json — the fact-check-safe set from TWO independent adversarial validators, with a binding cut_list. Everything is sourced from the ABSTRACT because the full text is paywalled (Wiley 402, pubs.usgs.gov 403), and that limitation must be disclosed in the Gmail draft.
angle.json — the earned angle, plus the thesis the validators KILLED so it is never re-derived.
storyboard.json — 32 beats and 12 shots, Gate 0A PASSING, timed against the real synthesized VO.
art_direction.json — the binding look plan (needs the Gate 0D numeric fixes still listed as open).
vo_script.txt + vo_direction.json + audio/vo.wav — THE VO IS ALREADY SYNTHESIZED AND PASSED QC at score 0.984, 96.7s, WER 0.023. Do NOT re-synth unless a line changes.
vo_lines.json + words.json + captions.json — correctly aligned after fixing an engine bug.
video-engine/src/lib/bench.tsx — AshReader, ShortlistCard, DistanceCalipers, CoreColumn, AshCrumbs.
video-engine/src/BenchLook.tsx — the look-dev sheet with a 0.28 legibility strip.
what_is_left: AshReader, DistanceCalipers and CoreColumn are NOT at the exemplar bar. The look-dev render shows the reader's head off its own bounding box and the body reading as a flat slab, the calipers reading as a flat V, and CoreColumn's name plates illegible at 0.28, which is the scale the poster frame uses. Taste-loop all three against BenchLook FIRST.

The remaining Gate 0B, 0C and 0D fixes that were not applied: numeric AccentRegistry rects in art_direction.json, the light plan's NightGrade values and depth-plane assignments, shot 2's light treatment, the glacier blade's actual construction (GlacierBG's serac edge is torn and it has no tint param, so the blade is net-new geometry and should be declared as such), and the TORN AGAINST TURNED exception for the cut notches.
Scene authoring for all 12 shots, the taste loop, the quality gates, the 3-judge panel, the ship gate, encode, upload, feed publish, the Gmail draft, and the merge.

unverified_note: Treat every figure and quote here as UNVERIFIED and re-check against claims.json, which is the only source of truth. The 2026-07-30 run proved a research summary can carry a fabricated quote into a package.

ALTERNATIVE_IF_YOU_WANT_A_FRESH_STORY.note: The angle room's skeptic filed a formal dissent that this is the bigger civic story on stakes, and it is time-sensitive.
ALTERNATIVE_IF_YOU_WANT_A_FRESH_STORY.headline: Alaska's $272,174,856 Rural Health Transformation year-one award began its subrecipient performance period on 2026-08-01, and the federal eligible-use language explicitly funds pilots of AI-enabled tools and wearables
ALTERNATIVE_IF_YOU_WANT_A_FRESH_STORY.key_facts: $272,174,856 year one, the second-largest state total and by far the largest per capita; roughly 1,800 proposals narrowed to just over 400; a Tanana Chiefs Conference plan to deliver vaccines and pharmaceuticals to Interior villages by drone; wearable blood-pressure monitors; VR healthcare-career training at Wrangell Public School District.
ALTERNATIVE_IF_YOU_WANT_A_FRESH_STORY.quote: You name a program 'transformation,' but the way that the feds designed it is almost directing us to AI. — Alaska state Rep. Genevieve Mina (D-Anchorage), member of the RHTP advisory council, via GovTech
ALTERNATIVE_IF_YOU_WANT_A_FRESH_STORY.caveat: The best reporting and the quote are from June 2026, so the in-window hook is the August 1 spending clock from the state's own page. Re-verify everything.
